summary: whether the mean of a series' last readings lies inside a band, between a lowest and a highest value it is handed

inputs.name: series
inputs.meaning: the readings in the order they were taken, all in one unit

inputs.name: window
inputs.meaning: how many of the last readings the mean takes

inputs.name: low
inputs.meaning: the lowest value inside the band, in the readings' unit; null when none is chosen

inputs.name: high
inputs.meaning: the highest value inside the band, in the readings' unit; null when none is chosen

outputs.name: last_mean
outputs.meaning: the mean of the last window, in the readings' unit; null when there are fewer readings than the window

validity: readings in one unit, the band in the same unit; the edges belong to the band

source.citation: a definition: inclusion in a closed interval; NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, Mathematical Introduction, Common Notations and Definitions (read 2026-11-17, https://dlmf.nist.gov/front/introduction; meta_agent/inbox/materials/20261117-nist-dlmf-introduction)
source.locus: Common Notations and Definitions: [a,b], the closed interval; the mean of the last readings lies in [low, high], the edges included

note: v1 with the definition it rests on named where it is defined, found by search; the code and the cases are v1's. No value of a source stands behind the worked cases: each is worked by hand in its worked field, on readings made up to show the comparison. v3 is v2 made common, unchanged in its code and its cases' values: every simulation bundle carries it (the person, 2026-11-18, docs/ideas/20261118.md; meta_agent/tasks/025), and each worked case names the kind of system it is worked on, at least two unrelated kinds. A build adapts it to an engine as a next version that names the engine and says adapted_from.
